title: Optimize Column Size
content: Column size for string data.  Go to Redshift service’s Query Editor interface.   We will perform a maximum length check of the columns based on the string. All string-based columns should not be given a larger size than necessary. It reduces the storage space on the Redshift cluster and also improves query performance when you use these columns in the query by consuming less memory.  select max(len(uuid)) as uuid_len, max(len(activity_type)) as activity_type_len from redshift_lab.f_raw_1;select max(len(track_name)) as uuid_len, max(len(artist_name)) as activity_type_len from redshift_lab.d_ref_data_1; The results from the above query will be used to determine the new precision for columns with string data.  Learn more about limiting column size here.

title: Compression
content:
Compression In this step, we will analyze the raw table to choose the appropriate compression algorithm.
 Check the appropriate algorithm on each table to perform compression. Compression is a column-level operation to reduce the size of data as it is stored. Compression helps optimize storage space and reduce the size of data read from storage, while reducing the amount of I/O to disk and improving query performance.   Run the following query in the Query Editor interface.  analyze compression redshift_lab.f_raw_1; The results from the table above provide the following information for each column:   Column Name Encoding: Recommended compression based on column type and precision value.  Est_reduction_pct: The estimated percentage reduction if the proposed compression method is implemented.

title: Writing Lambda Function Code
content:
Write Lambda Function code In this part, we will code for the lambda function we just created. We will use boto3 to access Athena.
Boto is the Amazon Web Services (AWS) SDK for Python. It allows Python developers to create, configure, and manage AWS services, such as EC2 and S3. Boto provides an easy-to-use, object-oriented API, as well as low-level access to AWS services. Read more about Boto here [https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/index.html?id=docs_gateway](https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/ latest/index.html?id=docs_gateway)
 Scroll down to the Function Code section and replace the code available in lambda_function.py with the python code below.  import boto3import timeimport os# Environment VariablesDATABASE = os.environ['DATABASE']TABLE = os.environ['TABLE']# Top X ConstantTOPX = 5# S3 ConstantS3_OUTPUT = f's3://{os.environ["BUCKET_NAME"]}/query_results/'# Number of RetriesRETRY_COUNT = 10def lambda_handler(event, context):client = boto3.client('athena')# query variable with two environment variables and a constantquery = f"""SELECT track_name as \"Track Name\", artist_name as \"Artist Name\",count(1) as \"Hits\" FROM {DATABASE}.{TABLE} GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 3 DESCLIMIT {TOPX};"""response = client.start_query_execution(QueryString=query,QueryExecutionContext={ 'Database': DATABASE },ResultConfiguration={'OutputLocation': S3_OUTPUT})query_execution_id = response['QueryExecutionId']# Get Execution Statusfor i in range(0, RETRY_COUNT):# Get Query Executionquery_status = client.get_query_execution(QueryExecutionId=query_execution_id)exec_status = query_status['QueryExecution']['Status']['State']if exec_status == 'SUCCEEDED':print(f'Status: {exec_status}')breakelif exec_status == 'FAILED':raise Exception(f'STATUS: {exec_status}')else:print(f'STATUS: {exec_status}')time.sleep(i)else:client.stop_query_execution(QueryExecutionId=query_execution_id)raise Exception('TIME OVER')# Get Query Resultsresult = client.get_query_results(QueryExecutionId=query_execution_id)print(result['ResultSet']['Rows'])# Function can return results to your application or service# return result['ResultSet']['Rows'] To configure the environment variable, click the Configuration tab.  Environment variables for Lambda functions allow you to move settings into your function code and libraries without making changes to your code. Read more about Lambda Environment Variables here [https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/env_variables.html](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg /env_variables.html)
 Click Environment variables. Click Edit.  Add 3 Environment variables below   Key: DATABASE, Value: analyticsworkshopdb. Key: TABLE, Value: processed_data. Key: BUCKET_NAME, Value: yourname-analytics-workshop-bucket. Click Save.  Click General Configuration.   Click Edit. Leave Memory (MB) as default 128 MB. Change Timeout to 10 seconds. Click Save.   Click Permissions.   Click the Role Name link to open the IAM Console in a new tab.  Click Attach policies  Add 2 policies as below:   ```AmazonS3FullAccess```` AmazonAthenaFullAccess  Once the policies have been attached, we can close this tab and return to the interface of the Lambda service.

title: Data Delivery
content:
Distribution Style and Sort Keys Distribution / Data distribution is an important performance optimization method on Redshift. Good data distribution reduces the amount of data that has to be moved back and forth between the nodes in the Redshift cluster.
 We will use a KEY based distribution for the f_raw_1 data table.   Since the two tables (f_raw_1 and d_ref_data_1) need to be merged on the track_id column, we will choose track_id as the distribution key.   We will use the ALL distribution for the dimension table - d_ref_data_1.
  Learn more about Redshift Distribution style here.
  In our queries, the activity_type attribute has been used to filter for equality, so we will choose this attribute as the sort column.
   Selecting a column that is often used to filter (filter) as a column to sort the data in the table will help the query become faster.  Learn more about Redshift’s best practices when using sort keys here

title: Create new table
content: Create a new table and transfer data to the new table.  Based on all the optimization steps we have evaluated, we will proceed to create a new table.   Create a new column using the DDL of f_raw_2 and d_ref_data_2  --fact table ddlCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS redshift_lab.f_raw_2 (uuid varchar(40) ENCODE zstd,device_ts timestamp,device_id int ENCODE az64,device_temp int ENCODE az64,track_id int ENCODE az64,activity_type varchar(16) ENCODE bytedict sortkey,load_time int ENCODE zstd)DISTKEY(track_id);--dimension table ddlCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS redshift_lab.d_ref_data_2 (track_id int,track_name varchar(64),artist_name varchar(64))DISTSTYLE ALL; Execute the following query to copy data from the old table to the new table.  --copy data from f_raw_1 to f_raw_2insert into redshift_lab.f_raw_2 select * from redshift_lab.f_raw_1;--copy data from d_ref_data_1 to d_ref_data_2INSERT into redshift_lab.d_ref_data_2 select * from redshift_lab.d_ref_data_1; Next we will perform additional cleaning and data analysis steps after moving to the new table.

ANALYZE: Update table statistics for use by query planner system, to optimize the way Redshift queries data.
Run the following query in the Query Editor.  vacuum redshift_lab.f_raw_2;analyze redshift_lab.f_raw_2; Continue  vacuum redshift_lab.d_ref_data_2;analyze redshift_lab.d_ref_data_2; Next, we will perform a data query on the new table after all the operations we have optimized.

title: Transform with DataBrew
content:
Transform Data with AWS Glue DataBrew What is AWS Glue DataBrew?
AWS Glue DataBrew is a visual data preparation tool that enables data analysts and data scientists to clean and normalize data in preparation for analytics and machine learning. You can choose from over 250 built-in data transformations to automate data prep work, without having to write any code.
You can automatically filter out data anomalies, convert data formats, and handle erroneous values ​​and other tasks. Once your data is ready, you can use it immediately for your analytics and machine learning projects. With Glue DataBrew you only pay for resources as you use them and require no upfront costs.
Content  Create DataBrew project Data profile with DataBrew Join dataset Initialize and run job Data Check

title: Create schema and tables
content: Create schema and Redshift tables  Go to Redshift service’s Query Editor interface .   At the Connect to database page. Select the Redshift cluster we created. Select Database name as dev, and Database user as admin. Click Connect.  Run the following queries to generate the schema.  -- Create redshift_lab schema.CREATE schema redshift_lab;  Run the following queries to create a table for raw and reference data.  -- Create f_raw_1 table.CREATE TABLE IF not EXISTS redshift_lab.f_raw_1 (uuid varchar(256),device_ts timestamp,device_id int,device_temp int,track_id int,activity_type varchar(128),load_time int); -- Create d_ref_data_1 table.CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS redshift_lab.d_ref_data_1 (track_id int,track_name varchar(128),artist_name varchar(128)); Next, we will perform the transformation and load the data into Redshift.

title: Query and performance comparison
content:
Run Query and compare performance  Execute the query below, listing 10 songs with the same artist performing for a certain type of activity.  selecttrack_name,artist_name,count(1) frequencyfromredshift_lab.f_raw_2 frinner joinredshift_lab.d_ref_data_2 drfonfr.track_id = drf.track_idwhereactivity_type = 'Running'group bytrack_name, artist_nameorder byfrequency desclimit 10; You can compare the execution time with the result of step 10.8 and compare the execution speed.   As on the image below, we can see that the execution time has been reduced from 12s to 2s for this query statement.  Congratulations on completing the Data Analytics workshop on AWS. Hope this workshop will familiarize you with the services and features that make it easier to build data analytics solutions on AWS. .
